title: Mexico Announces 12,750 Primary Care Clinics for 2027
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [August 25, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/gobierno-
anuncia-12-mil-750-consultorios-de-atencion-primaria-para-2027/), a Mexican
investigative journalism magazine._

The federal government will expand its **primary health care** network with
**12,750 new clinics** in the 24 states where IMSS-Bienestar operates. The new
infrastructure will begin operating in **January 2027** and, according to the
Ministry of Health, will add **40 million consultations** for the population.

The Undersecretary for Sectoral Integration and Coordination of Medical Care
Services, **Eduardo Clark** , explained during the morning press conference
that the clinics aim to bring medical services closer to people and treat low-
complexity conditions, as well as follow up on chronic degenerative diseases
such as **diabetes and hypertension**.

The new spaces will be installed in both urban and rural areas, based on
identifying places where medical care points are currently lacking or where
existing capacity needs to be expanded. For this, **Health Houses, clinics,
workplaces, and IMSS Family Medicine Units** , among other spaces, are being
considered.

The official noted that the clinics will have a **standardized care model**
across the 24 states. They will also have medical staff able to prescribe
medications, as well as basic equipment and technological tools, including
computers, internet, and an **Electronic Medical Record**.

He detailed that these spaces will treat acute conditions requiring immediate
care, such as a cold, diarrhea, or mild pain, but will also serve for the
prevention and control of chronic diseases.

In addition, each clinic will have **90 types of free medications** , selected
by specialists from the Ministry of Health, the IMSS, the ISSSTE, and IMSS-
Bienestar to treat the main primary-care conditions. The planned hours will be
**8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on weekdays** , while on weekends they will operate
from **8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.**

For his part, the Minister of Health, **David Kershenobich** , explained that
primary care seeks to keep patients from having to go directly to hospitals
for conditions that can be resolved at a first level of care.

> “Primary health care is the closest point where the population can receive
> care; it is the gateway to the Health System.”
>
> David KerShenObich

According to the official, this model will also improve follow-up of people
with **diabetes and hypertension** , carry out prevention and vaccination
actions, and follow up on pregnant women and children.

If medical staff detect a serious condition, the patient may be **referred to
higher-level care units** , including IMSS-Bienestar, IMSS, or ISSSTE
hospitals.

The expansion of the clinics will be linked to the **Universal Health
Service** , through an app that will allow users to manage appointments, check
their medical history, review prescriptions, and have an electronic medical
record.

Undersecretary Clark also reported that a **National Teleconsultation Center**
is planned, with **1,000 doctors** available to provide remote care from
users’ homes or workplaces.

The official noted that access to the new clinics will be universal within the
24 states where IMSS-Bienestar operates. That is, a person will be able to go
to a clinic regardless of whether their coverage corresponds to IMSS, ISSSTE,
or IMSS-Bienestar.

The launch of the clinics will be accompanied by a community process. Starting
**September 14** , the **Health for Well-being Committees** will begin to be
formed; they will receive resources and verify the necessary adaptations to
the spaces.

Also, from **September 14 to October 31** , a call will be open to hire the
staff who will work at these clinics. It will be aimed at doctors, nurses, and
technical and auxiliary health personnel.

He added that **retired doctors and nurses** may also participate, joining the
program without suspending their pension payments. The federal government
expects the network to begin operating in **January 2027** and to be ready
between January and February of that year.
